newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK gold ends down on producer sales.
newsitem.headline: HK gold ends down on producer sales.

text.p: Hong Kong gold ended down on Tuesday from New York's previous close on producer selling, but activity during the day was lethargic, bullion traders said.
"Australian producers were selling," said one bullion source.
Others reported slow interest from Japanese and Hong Kong clients.
Bullion ended at US$352.00/30 an ounce against New York's US$353.00/50 close on Monday.
Market sentiment turned bearish after gold failed to break through $355 and was marked by confusion and uncertainty, some traders said.
Bullion dealers were divided over the price direction, with some betting gold would drop below $350 this week and others predicting firmness.
Steady physical demand continued to lend support to prices and, according to some traders, the supply tightness in Hong Kong was easing.
Local gold ended HK$3 higher at HK$3,257 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged from its previous fix at nil.
